desc:
Given an integer array nums that may contain negative numbers, and an integer k (which may also be negative), return the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is at most k. If no non-empty subarray qualifies, return 0.

Careful: with negative numbers the usual two-pointer window no longer works, because removing an element from the left can make the sum larger.

nums = [4, -3, 2, -1, 5], k = 2
[-3, 2, -1] sums to -2, and [4, -3, 2, -1] sums to 2
result = 4
hints: Test the window idea on [5, -10, 1] with a small k: when the sum is too large, is dropping the leftmost element guaranteed to help?
Switch to prefix sums P. A subarray (i, j] has sum P[j] - P[i], so you need the smallest i < j with P[i] ≥ P[j] - k.

The smallest such i is always a new running maximum of the prefix sums (every earlier prefix is smaller than the target). Keep those running-maximum prefixes in a list; their values increase, so binary search finds the first one that is large enough.
editorial: Without sign restrictions the sum of a window is not monotone in either end, so shrinking from the left cannot be trusted. Use prefix sums instead: the subarray between prefix indices i < j has sum P[j] - P[i], and it is acceptable when P[i] ≥ P[j] - k. For each j we want the smallest such i.

Let i* be the smallest index with P[i*] ≥ target. Every earlier prefix is smaller than the target and therefore smaller than P[i*], so i* is a strict prefix maximum. Store only the strict prefix maxima (indices and values, both increasing) and binary-search the target among the values. This is a sliding-window-style idea (best left end for each right end) with the monotonic structure supplied by prefix maxima. Time O(n log n), space O(n).
solution:
def longestSumAtMostWithNegatives(nums, k):
    from bisect import bisect_left
    idxs = []
    vals = []
    pref = 0
    prefix = [0]
    for x in nums:
        pref += x
        prefix.append(pref)
    best = 0
    for j in range(1, len(prefix)):
        i = j - 1
        if not vals or prefix[i] > vals[-1]:
            idxs.append(i)
            vals.append(prefix[i])
        pos = bisect_left(vals, prefix[j] - k)
        if pos < len(vals):
            best = max(best, j - idxs[pos])
    return best
